The core idea

Three alphabets, one grammar

Almost everything in a horoscope is generated from three small sets and a few "states." You don't memorize meanings — you build them.

What this app is. Jyotish Atlas teaches the classical grammar of Vedic astrology and applies it to a chart, following texts such as BPHS. Its readings describe tendencies and themes as that tradition sees them. They aren’t predictions of fixed events, and nothing here is medical, financial or legal advice.

The costumes — how it expresses (the sign's flavor)

A Graha× a Rashi× a Bhava→ one specific meaning

9 × 12 × 12 = 1,296 base placements — each shifting again with dignity, divisional charts and aspect. You can't memorize that. You derive it. Try the Synthesizer.

Alphabet 1 · the actors

The 9 Grahas

Each planet is a character with a fixed nature and a bundle of significations (karakatvas). Click one to meet it.

Alphabet 2 · the costumes

The 12 Rashis

A sign doesn't do things — it colors whatever planet stands in it, through its element, modality and ruler.

Alphabet 3 · the stages

The 12 Bhavas

Houses are areas of life. Whatever planet sits here pours its nature into these themes.

Lunar mansions · fine grain

The 27 Nakshatras

Nakshatras are the Moon's 27 stations: the subtle layer beneath sign placement. Select one for its symbol, ruling deity, motivation, yoni, naming sounds, strengths and shadow — the fine grain that colours any graha placed there.

Alphabet 5 · putting it together

The Cosmic Body

Classical texts lay the zodiac over a human figure, the Kālapuruṣa or “Time-Person”: Aries is the head and Pisces the feet. Seeing signs, houses and nakshatras on one body is the quickest way to remember their order. Select any part of the body, a house or a nakshatra.

Planets · Dignity · Functional Nature · Nakshatra

Divisional Charts (Varga) · Shodasavarga

Each D-N magnifies one domain of life (hover a column header). A planet strong across many vargas truly delivers; strong in D-1 but weak in the divisions is a promise that fades. ◆ gold = vargottama — same sign in D-1 and that varga, a major strength. Viṁśopaka Bala (Ṣaḍvarga · /20) weights D-1·6, D-2·2, D-3·4, D-9·5, D-12·2, D-30·1 by dignity in each.

Jaimini · Chara Kārakas, Kārakāṁśa & Argala

The Chara Kārakas are movable significators: the planet at the highest degree in its sign becomes the Ātmakāraka (soul significator), and the rest fall in order of descending degree.

Chara Kārakas
Kārakāṁśa
Argala on the Lagna — who intervenes in your selfhood (effective when the intervening house outnumbers its obstruction)

Planetary Avasthas · states of a planet

A planet can be well-placed yet unable to deliver. Bālādi reads its life-stage by degree (peaks at Yuvā), Jāgradādi its wakefulness, Dīptādi its condition. Effective strength leads with dignity across D-1, D-9 & D-10 plus vargottama — the primary strength — and only modulates by avastha, so an exalted, own-sign or vargottama planet stays strong even at a weak degree. The notes flag where promise (D-1) and delivery (D-9 / D-10) diverge. Use the D-1 … D-60 tabs to read each planet's dignity & avasthā in any divisional chart — combustion is carried from D-1 (vargas have no degrees).

Bhinna Ashtakavarga (BAV) — benefic points per house

Each cell shows how many benefic points (0–8) that planet contributes to that house. ∑ SAV is the house total across all 7 planets (≥30 strong, 25–29 average, <25 weak). Gold outline = planet's natal house.

5–8 strong 4 solid 3 average 2 weak 0–1 very weak outlined = natal house

Relationship decoder

Every person in your life maps to a specific house. Any topic about that person maps to another house counted forward from there — bhavat bhavam, "from house to house." Jaimini · Planetary Reflections

Graha Arudhas

Each planet has a Graha Arudha — the material, external reflection of that planet's archetype. Since most planets rule two signs, they each cast two Arudhas. The rule (BPHS Ch.32): count how many signs the planet's owned sign is from the planet itself, then count that same number forward from the planet. Where this reflection lands is where that planetary energy — solar authority, lunar emotion, Martian drive — manifests as a visible, tangible force in your world. The final cluster analysis shows which houses receive the most reflections, revealing the dominant material arenas of your life.

Add a chart in My Charts above to compute Graha Arudhas.
Nakshatra sūtra · profession & livelihood

Career Decoder

Saturn is the kāraka of karma — the work you actually do. This sūtra reads the chain rather than the planet: Saturn → the nakshatra it sits in → that nakshatra's lord → the rāśi and bhāva that lord occupies. The rāśi names the domain of the work; the bhāva names how and where it is delivered; the dispositor and the planets aspecting that lord add the flavours. Swap the kāraka to run the same chain for money, learning or the mind.

Add a chart in My Charts above to decode the career chain.
Upachaya sūtra · timing

Opportunity Windows

Houses 3, 6, 10 and 11 — the upachaya or growth houses — are where life hands you openings. Counted not from the Lagna but from the kāraka of the thing you want: Moon for opportunity in general, Venus for money, Jupiter for expansion, Mercury for business, Sun for vitality. Any planet sitting in those four houses from that kāraka will hand you an opening — and it does so when its daśā or antardaśā runs. This finds those planets and dates their windows.

Add a chart in My Charts above to find your opportunity windows.

When is the right time?

Jupiter and Saturn move slowly — roughly one sign per year and 2.5 years respectively. Where they land against your natal houses, crossed with SAV, reveals your strongest windows for each goal.

Horary · praśna

Prashna Kundli

No birth chart? Ask a question and cast a chart for the exact moment and place you ask it — the classical horary method. The rising sign, the Moon, and the house of your matter carry the answer. Cast it the instant the question feels most alive in your mind.

📖 Praśna technique — the querent & outcome are read from the Lagna & its lord, the mind from the Moon, and the matter from its significator house (BPHS / Prashna Marga principle). The Lagna is computed from local sidereal time, obliquity & latitude; planets from this app's own ephemeris; both made sidereal with the Lahiri ayanāṃśa. Horary is an aid to reflection — treat the leaning as an indication, not a verdict.
Your data loop · patterns over time

Life Journal

Log real events from your life — a job change, a move, a marriage, an illness, a windfall. Each one is tagged with the Mahādaśā / Antardaśā and the slow-planet transits that were running that day, so your own patterns emerge across the years. This is a journal for noticing, not a proof engine.

Practice — decode the sky

Quick questions drawn from the blocks you just met. Reasoning beats memorizing — every answer shows why.

About the content. Significations, dignities, lordships, Navamsa & aspects follow the classical Brihat Parashara Hora Shastra. Chapter numbering varies by edition, so references are by topic. Rahu/Ketu exaltation differs between authorities and is noted. The Career Decoder and Opportunity Windows sections apply two teaching sūtras — reading a kāraka through its nakshatra lord, and counting the upachaya from a kāraka rather than from the Lagna. Both are built on standard Parashari components (nakshatra lordship, whole-sign houses, dispositors, Vimshottari), but the sūtras themselves are taught technique rather than a direct BPHS citation, and each is one thread of a chart, not the whole reading. Your pasted charts are stored only in this browser (localStorage).
